transcript:
kai: Quick follow-up from the v3 FlashAttention rollout — seeing weird perf deltas on short sequences after kernel selection changes.

kai: Observed on nightly canary (dedicated pool) after enabling v3 by default for models >= 3B

maria: Details? numbers and workload shape please :eyes:

kai: p50 token latency for seq=32, batch=1 increased from ~12ms -> ~22ms on A100s
kai: throughput for seq=512 steady, so this looks short-seq specific
kai: repro script attached in thread (quick snippet):

kai: ```bash
# repro client
for i in {1..100}; do curl -sS -X POST $HOST/generate -d '{"input":"hello"}'; done
```

david: Did we fall back to a generic gemm kernel for tiny head counts? v3 sometimes misses the narrow-MHA opt

priya: We saw similar before — kernel picker prefers v3 flash for large seq, but heuristic uses workspace estimate and sometimes rejects v3 for tiny seq+high heads

maria: Can we dump the kernel-choice telemetry for the exact requests? head_count=32, heads_per_head=... need all tags

kai: I pulled a few traces:
- request 1768456789.1: model xg-7b, seq=32, batch=1, heads=32, dtype=bf16 -> selected: fa_v3, but used fallback path internally for matmul
- request 1768456789.7: model xg-7b, seq=32, batch=1, heads=64, dtype=fp16 -> selected: fa_v2

david: That first one indicates we picked fa_v3 front-end but failed kernel negotiation and fell back. Do we surface a fallback metric? I only see success counters.

priya: Not reliably. We log a single chosen_kernel tag, but not the internal negotiated fragment. Need an explicit "negotiated_path" field

sre-bot: deploy: canary rollout at 2026-02-12T22:03Z, 27% hosts

maria: Also check allocator fragmentation — fa_v3 relies on contiguous workspace sizes; small seq sometimes triggers extra cudaMalloc and stalls

kai: Good call. I saw spikes in cudaMalloc latency correlated with fallbacks.

david: Proposed fixes:
- add negotiated_path telemetry (fa_v3/full, fa_v3/fallback-gemm, fa_v2, generic_gemm)
- add fast-path check earlier to avoid doing heavy workspace allocs when we know fallback will be used
- tighten kernel selector to prefer v2 for (seq<64 && heads>=32 && dtype==bf16)

priya: I like telemetry + early reject. Kernel selector rules are getting messy though — maybe we need a declarative cost model instead of handcrafted heuristics.

maria: Agree. Short-term: telemetry + early rejection + a canary toggle for per-model kernel policy.

kai: Short-term telemetry patch landed in my branch, pushing perf counters to traces. Can someone review the sampling overhead? It adds ~0.4ms to p99 in worst-case when enabled.

david: 0.4ms is ok for debugging but need to gate it under a sampling flag enabled only for 1% of requests by default.

priya: Also add a lightweight offline profiler: run a microbench of all kernel variants on representative shapes during model upload and use that as a prior for selector.

maria: That could remove runtime negotiation cost entirely for most customer models. We already have an upload hook in the private deploy flow.

kai: Action items:
- kai: push telemetry -> canary sampling 1% (in review)
- david: prototype declarative cost rules + simple threshold for short-seq fallback
- priya: microbench harness for model upload path
- maria: add dashboard widgets to surface negotiated_path breakdowns and cudaMalloc failure spikes

david: One more note: quantized kernels (int8/qint4) also have different constraints. Ensure negotiated_path includes quantized tag when available.

kai: Repro steps and raw logs pasted to the debugging sprint ticket: https://redwood.atlassian/browse/INF-4321

maria: I'll schedule a 30m sync tomorrow to go over telemetry schema so we don't iterate on incompatible tags.

priya: Can we tentatively roll the v3 default back to previous heuristic for short-seq until fixes land? I don't want customers hitting regressions in PLG layer.

kai: I'll prepare a quick rollout patch to pin old selector for models < 6B and seq<64. Not ideal long-term but buys time.

sre-bot: note: rollback patch scheduled at 2026-02-13T03:00Z if not approved

kai: Thanks all. I'll post updates here after the canary runs with telemetry enabled.

maria: Thanks — great triage. :thumbsup:
